source.title: Contrast to Divide: Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Evgenii Zheltonozhskii; Chaim Baskin; A. Mendelson; A. Bronstein; O. Litany

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no obvious truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Applies self-supervised pre-training and noisy-label learning to CIFAR, Clothing1M, and WebVision settings, measuring warm-up features, loss separation, and downstream performance. It does not run the random-label or unstructured-input experiments in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior findings about memorization and noise robustness, but those citations are not extracted as this study's results. Its own rows cover feature quality and loss separation under noisy labels, and the reported consequence of ImageNet pre-training for LNL; the CIFAR, Clothing1M, WebVision, and semi-supervised accuracy comparisons do not directly measure the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses early learning before noise memorization to motivate noisy-label detection and mitigation. Its own results measure feature quality, noise-detection ROC-AUC, loss separation and downstream accuracy, rather than random-label fitting or the temporal order of learning real and noisy labels. The record's T3 classification is therefore inappropriate.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that self-supervised pre-training improves warm-up feature quality and loss separation, reduces sensitivity to noise, and improves existing noisy-label methods without external labeled data. They leave the sources of neural-network robustness and better use of pre-trained features as open questions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses self-supervised pre-training followed by noisy-label learning; it does not use the original random-label fitting intervention or measure its outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise level changes warm-up feature quality and separation; the reported ImageNet-pre-training outcome also varies by method and setting. The text notes tuning of DivideMix hyperparameters and training length.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 3 and 6.1 report that warm-up feature quality and noise-detection separability peak together and deteriorate with increasing noise. C2D improves both; Figure 3 shows cleaner separation of clean and noisy sample losses after warm-up.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-supervised pre-training improves representation quality and clean/noisy loss separation during noisy-label learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1–5 report improved noisy-label classification performance with C2D. Section 6.2 reports that ImageNet initialization can instead reduce performance, including ELR+ accuracy falling from 60.8% to 48.58% at 80% CIFAR-100 noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of pre-training for noisy-label learning depends on the pre-training approach and downstream method.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The study does not test the listed random-label, unstructured-input, or memorization-order claims. Several warm-up comparisons are presented as figures without exact numeric values in the supplied text. Some comparison results are sourced from prior published work or code, as noted by the authors.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: the reported results concern noisy-label learning and pre-training, not the behaviors named by V1–V6.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance and unchanged training settings.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across a corruption sweep and simultaneous test-error degradation toward chance; downstream noisy-label accuracy alone does not establish this.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Direct comparison over training of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels. Epoch-wise feature quality and detection ROC-AUC do not establish that learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The original-source learning-order finding is cited and used, rather than directly retested. No qualifying rows need adding: rows_left_out already declares the feature-quality, detection and downstream-performance results outside V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random-label training experiment or test error at chance.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or sweep over corruption fraction for that purpose.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
No experiment tests perfect training fit across label-noise rates while measuring test error toward chance.
Does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels or whether their removal harms generalization.
Does not compare learning order of shared real-data patterns and noisy or random labels over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
